Article Title: 'Not fluent in Tamil is an insult': Actor Dhanush pushes for mother tongue first
Article Text:
Dhanush's strong pitch for Tamil

NEW DELHI: Actor Dhanush has renewed the focus on the language debate with his remarks stressing the importance of learning Tamil and being "fluent in one's mother tongue."Speaking at an event, the actor strongly backed the Tamil language and urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue.Recalling his school days, Dhanush said, "When I was in school, we were fluent in Tamil and we struggled with English. Now the situation is opposite."He added, "Now, out of the 10 people I meet, eight don't know Tamil. One should be fluent in their mother tongue before everything else. To say I'm not fluent in Tamil is not a matter of pride. It's an insult. Focus on learning Tamil language."His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu, where the issue has frequently put the state government at odds with the Centre. Leaders across the state's political spectrum, from DMK chief and former CM MK Stalin to TVK founder and CM Vijay, have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.
Article Summary: Actor Dhanush has urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue. His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu. Leaders across the state's political spectrum have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.

Article Title: Bombay high court convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal
Article Text:
Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Thursday convicted former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal in the 2013 rape case filed by his former junior colleague, overturning his acquittal by a Goa trial court.The verdict came nearly 13 years after the alleged incident during the ThinkFest event in Goa, where Tejpal was accused of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator. The high court had reserved its judgment last week after hearing arguments from both sides.The Goa government had challenged Tejpal's acquittal after a sessions court cleared him of all charges in May 2021. The appeal was heard by Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar of the Bombay high court's Goa bench, which had directed Tejpal to remain present for the pronouncement of the verdict.Appearing for the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had argued that the trial court committed a serious error by evaluating the complainant's conduct based on preconceived notions of how a survivor of sexual assault should behave.He submitted that there is no universal standard governing the reaction of a sexual assault survivor, as responses vary depending on an individual's education, personality, social background and circumstances.Tejpal, who was present in court, sought leniency, claiming that he was a "political victim" and the father of two daughters.Mehta also argued that the trial court placed undue emphasis on minor inconsistencies in the complainant's statements instead of examining whether her core allegations remained consistent.Referring to an email sent by Tejpal to the complainant after the alleged incident, the Solicitor General argued that the accused had apologised for his "lapse of judgment", expressed shame and stated that he believed the encounter had been consensual. According to the prosecution, those statements amounted to an admission that an encounter had taken place.The defence, led by senior advocate Abad Ponda, argued that the prosecution had misread the apology emails as admissions of a sexual encounter.Ponda submitted that none of the emails contained any admission of a consensual physical or sexual encounter and that the references related only to a consensual verbal conversation of a sexual nature.The defence also questioned the complainant's credibility, arguing that her conduct before and after the alleged incident, along with emails, WhatsApp messages and documentary evidence, contradicted the prosecution's case.The high court's conviction reverses the trial court's acquittal, with sentencing to be decided after hearing arguments on the quantum of punishment.
Article Summary: The verdict came nearly 13 years after the alleged incident during the ThinkFest event in Goa. Tejpal was accused of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator. The high court's conviction reverses the trial court's acquittal. sentencing to be decided after hearing arguments on the quantum of punishment.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET protest crackdown, says students were forced to apologise
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET crackdown

NEW DELHI: Standing with a group of youngsters who faced police action during the NEET protests , Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Wednesday said the ruling party is sending goons to the homes of students and forcing them to apologise, after which those apologies are being accepted by the PM.“There is no question of the youngsters apologising… I am very proud of them and what thousands of them did… They defended the Constitution and protected the idea of India and India’s future,” Rahul said.The Congress leader held a “freewheeling” discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. It included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks” at Jantar Mantar on July 20. Farah Naaz alleged that in police detention, she faced communal barbs with a cop even calling her “anti-national”. Muskan said she was being assumed to be a Muslim which makes an Indian a “fair game”, even clarifying that she is a Hindu. Nutan Toppo said a pellet gun was fired at her.The leader of opposition’s decision to meet the youngsters to 10, Janpath, for a chat further upped the ante in the “BJP vs opposition” confrontation that has jammed the ongoing monsoon session of parliament.Continuing its aggression, a large contingent of opposition MPs marched inside the Parliament complex to protest the “absence of Amit Shah from parliament” and “Ayodhya donation scam”. The group included Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Dimple Yadav, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Dharmendra Yadav, Supriya Sule, NK Premachandran, Sagarika Ghose, Amar Singh, Chowdry Mohd Ramzan, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Naseer Hussain, K Radhakrishnan.Rahul held a placard with a face riddled with pellet gun injuries and a question “who gave the order?” The members also sought statehood for J&K.Addressing the media with the youngsters, Rahul said, “They are so young and standing before the media. But the prime minister and the home minister have no courage to stand before the press."He attacked home minister Amit Shah by saying that he is responsible for the crackdown on youngsters but “he does not have the decency to come to the Parliament, and the courage to comment on what happened.”Rahul took a jibe at PM Narendra Modi for saying that he has forgiven the students.
Article Summary: The Congress leader held a “freewheeling’ discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. The group included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks”

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday claimed that Meta had restricted his Instagram account in India without providing any explanation. He alleged that repeated attempts to seek clarification from the company's India office had gone unanswered.In a post on X, Kejriwal tagged Meta and Meta India, saying his account had become unavailable to users in India."Hi @Meta @metaindia Why have you restricted my account? Verbal enquiries at your India office revealed that my account has been restricted in India and is unavailable in India. Why? Noone in your office is giving any reasons. Noone is suggesting how restrictions can be removed. All emails written have elicited no response other than routine acknowledgement. Thats pretty bad service. Don’t bow down to our Prime Minister so much. Else he will allow u to run only his own account in India," he said.Kejriwal alleged that officials at Meta's India office informed him verbally about the restriction but did not disclose the reason behind the action or explain how it could be reversed. He also claimed that emails sent to the company had received only routine acknowledgements.The AAP leader further accused Meta of "bowing down" to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging political bias in the platform's actions.Kejriwal's allegation comes a day after Meta apologised to the government over the erroneous removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video from Facebook. The company attributed the incident to a technical error, with Meta's chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan saying he had apologised to Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on behalf of the company.The apology followed a parliamentary panel's warning that Meta could risk losing its intermediary "safe harbour" protection if it failed to explain the removal of the Prime Minister's video. During discussions with the government, Meta also acknowledged lapses related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deepfakes and paid content amplification, while assuring authorities that corrective measures would be implemented.Meta has not yet publicly responded to Kejriwal's latest claims regarding the alleged restriction of his Instagram account.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal claims that Meta had restricted his Instagram account in India. He alleged that repeated attempts to seek clarification from the company's India office had gone unanswered. Kejriwal's allegation comes a day after Meta apologised to the government over the erroneous removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video from Facebook.

Article Title: Air India turbulence lasted 'four to five minutes'; some passengers still in hospital
Article Text:
Some passengers still in hospital

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India's recent severe turbulence incident is now under a "thorough investigation" by the directorate general of civil aviation (DGCA), civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Wednesday.Naidu said the Air India flight from Phuket to New Delhi experienced severe turbulence for "four to five minutes", leaving several passengers injured and some crew members with spinal and neck injuries.At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude during the midair turbulence.Addressing the media, Naidu said the aircraft was secured immediately after landing and all crucial evidence has been taken into the regulator's custody."In terms of why the incident has happened, we have immediately alerted the DGCA to thoroughly investigate the situation. The moment the plane was landed, it was put in a separate hangar. The data recorder, the voice recorder, everything is in the possession of DGCA. They will thoroughly investigate how and why this incident happened. Only when we have the facts in front of us, we are going to make it public," he said.The minister said medical teams attended to passengers and crew immediately after the flight landed in Delhi."The moment the flight landed in Delhi, the medical assistance team immediately attended to them. All first aid and medical assistance that needed to be provided was done at the airport itself. There were some passengers and crew members who were observed to need more medical assistance, they were shifted to Medanta Hospital and also Fortis Hospital," Naidu added.He said seven passengers admitted to Medanta Hospital on Monday were discharged after undergoing medical examinations."Spinal Injuries Centre, Fortis Centre - two passsengers were admitted yesterday. They both were also discharged but four crew members were admitted in Fortis where I also personally visited along with Ministry Team and DGCA Team. We interacted with crew members also. They have been very brave, even after that incident happened for 5 minutes and they were prone to certain injuries, the plane had to travel for 1 more hour. Even through that hour, the crew members provided all the assistance that was required. So, it was very brave of the women, the crew members who were on the flight," he said.The Airbus A320neo, operating as flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi on Tuesday, was carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members. Following the turbulence, 13 passengers and four crew members sustained injuries and were taken to hospitals for medical evaluation.According to Air India, as of 6:50 pm, five passengers had been discharged, while the remaining injured continued to receive treatment and care.An Air India spokesperson said on Tuesday, "Earlier today, Air India flight AI2379 operating from Phuket to Delhi experienced a sudden loss of altitude during cruise. After the momentary event, the aircraft continued normally and landed safely in Delhi at 11:07 hrs IST."The DGCA is now investigating the incident to determine the cause of the severe midair turbulence.
Article Summary: At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude during midair turbulence. Civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said the aircraft was secured immediately after landing and all crucial evidence has been taken into the regulator's custody.

Article Title: Centre deploys national team as Chandipura outbreak probe intensifies
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With 35 laboratory-confirmed Chandipura virus infections and 22 deaths among 184 suspected cases reported in children under 15 across Gujarat this monsoon, and the virus also affecting children from neighbouring Rajasthan, the Centre on Wednesday deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to strengthen outbreak investigations and accelerate scientific efforts to contain the disease.Chandipura virus, a sandfly-borne virus that primarily affects children, can rapidly progress from fever to acute encephalitis syndrome (AES), a severe brain infection. While sandflies are the established vector, scientists are investigating whether mosquitoes, ticks or mites may also be involved in the current outbreak.The virus is not new to India. First identified in Chandipura village in Maharashtra in 1965, it has caused periodic outbreaks of acute encephalitis among children in states such as Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, particularly during the monsoon.The multidisciplinary team, comprising experts from the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), will support state authorities in outbreak investigation, epidemiological assessment, laboratory coordination, clinical management and vector surveillance. The NCDC's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre has also been activated to coordinate the response.Rajasthan has stepped up surveillance after children from the state, including a two-year-old girl, tested positive for Chandipura virus while undergoing treatment in Gujarat. The cross-border cases prompted the Centre to include Rajasthan in its coordinated response.The deployment comes amid one of the country's most extensive scientific investigations into Chandipura virus in recent years, involving multiple ICMR institutes, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC). Scientists are trying to answer key questions about the virus's transmission, clinical spectrum and evolution while generating evidence to guide public health measures.Surveillance has been intensified among patients with acute febrile illness (AFI) and acute encephalitis syndrome, while community serosurveys are underway to estimate the extent of asymptomatic infections. Researchers are also analysing samples from sandflies, mosquitoes, ticks and mites to identify the vector responsible for the current outbreak.At the same time, blood and milk samples from cattle, buffaloes and goats are being tested to determine whether domestic animals could act as virus reservoirs.Around 70 animal blood samples have been collected so far and are being analysed for Chandipura virus and other relevant pathogens.Scientists are also carrying out whole-genome sequencing of virus samples to determine whether the circulating strain has undergone genetic changes. Officials said findings from the investigation, together with data generated through India's hospital-based Acute Encephalitis Syndrome surveillance network, will strengthen outbreak detection, improve understanding of the disease and support evidence-based public health interventions.
Article Summary: Chandipura virus, a sandfly-borne virus that primarily affects children, can rapidly progress from fever to acute encephalitis syndrome. 22 deaths among 184 suspected cases reported in children under 15 across Gujarat this monsoon. The virus also affecting children from neighbouring Rajasthan.

Article Title: Jharkhand protests: Five-member student panel to hold talks with Soren govt today - key points
Article Text:
The state government has repeatedly stressed its willingness to engage with the protesters.

Here are the top developments:

Students agree to talks, but seek public meeting

Government says doors are open

Probe gathers pace as arrests rise

NEW DELHI: Students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand have agreed in principle to hold talks with the state government, provided the discussions take place in the presence of the media. The development came even as the Crime Investigation Department (CID) arrested five more people in connection with the alleged recruitment scam, taking the investigation forward.Student leader Radhe Kumar said a five-member core committee would attend the meeting with government representatives. "Five members of our core team will attend the meeting. We will present our demands to the government through the SDO, who will convey them to the appropriate authorities. Once the government responds to our demands, we will decide our next course of action," he said.Student leaders said they were prepared to send a four- or five-member delegation for discussions after receiving a message from the government through the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO). However, they insisted that the talks should be transparent."We also had another demand: if the chief minister comes out to speak with us publicly in front of live media on an open platform, a proper resolution could be reached.In our previous protest, our representatives were taken into a closed room, and nothing came out of it. They are calling a five-member team just to stall and suppress our movement," one protester alleged.Another protester echoed the demand, saying, "The chief minister should listen to the students' demands in front of the press and media, and whatever promises he intends to fulfil should be stated publicly. For the last 26 years in Jharkhand, students' issues have been heard in closed rooms, and the files have remained closed forever."Student leader Ravindra Paswan said both sides had shown willingness to engage."The government has expressed its willingness to engage in dialogue, and we have also conveyed our willingness. Dialogue is essential in a democratic country as it is the only way to reach a resolution," Paswan said.He added that the students had placed two conditions before the government."Our primary condition is that the dialogue should take place directly with the chief minister, and we have been assured that the chief minister will be present. Secondly, we want at least two media representatives to be present during the discussions. The SDO has asked us to submit the names of our delegation members before 10 am, after which the date and time of the meeting will be communicated," he said.The state government has repeatedly stressed its willingness to engage with the protesters.Jharkhand minister Irfan Ansari said, "The chief minister has constituted the committee... We have opened the door for dialogue. Talks will take place, we will listen to your demands, and if they are reasonable, we will certainly accept them. They are our students, our children." He also accused the BJP of trying to politicise the issue.Rural development minister Deepika Pandey Singh said a committee had been formed and students had been asked to nominate their representatives so discussions could begin.However, Finance Minister Radhakrishna Kishore clarified that the ministers' group was only monitoring the agitation and was not a formal negotiation committee. He said the chief minister remained sensitive to the students' concerns and that the government was ready for talks whenever the students decided to engage.Earlier this week, chief minister Hemant Soren also said the government was open to dialogue and assured students that their demands would be considered seriously."...Many individuals have already been arrested and sent to jail, and investigative agencies are conducting raids at multiple locations. Overall, the agencies are working diligently and effectively on this matter, and I believe we will move forward towards a concrete resolution..." he said."The government's doors are open to everyone. Anyone who has demands can come forward and present their concerns. We are already aware of the issues to some extent, and if they present their views, the government will certainly consider them seriously," he added.The CID's latest action saw five more arrests in connection with the alleged examination irregularities, taking the total number of arrests to 19.The investigation is being led by an SIT, which is examining digital records, application logs and other evidence to establish the extent of the alleged recruitment irregularities.On August 5, Soren also met Governor Santosh Gangwar and briefed him on the alleged irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC examinations as well as the ongoing protests. The Governor described the allegations as a serious matter and stressed the need for a transparent examination process to maintain the confidence of young job aspirants.According to an official release, Soren assured the Governor that the state government was committed to ensuring justice for students and that no injustice would be allowed.The protests began after the results of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination were declared on July 5. Aspirants have since been staging round-the-clock demonstrations and an indefinite sit-in, demanding cancellation of the preliminary examination and a review of recruitment tests conducted through TDPL agencies.
Article Summary: Students agree in principle to hold talks with the state government, provided the discussions take place in the presence of the media. The development came even as the Crime Investigation Department (CID) arrested five more people in connection with the alleged recruitment scam, taking the investigation forward.

Article Title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher to school gate, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
Article Text:
Footage shows accused lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think should be done to better prevent stalking-related crimes? Stricter laws against stalking Faster action on complaints More public awareness campaigns 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GURGAON: A stalker who allegedly pursued a 26-year-old teacher for nearly two years walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name, and then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent.Captured on CCTV cameras, the attack unfolded in seconds and left the young English teacher dead before she could be taken to hospital.The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village in Faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking Sandhya, who taught at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona, and attacked her after she allegedly severed all contact with him and warned him she would approach police if he continued to harass her.Amit entered the school around 9.30am, his face partially covered with a scarf, and asked staff to inform Sandhya that “Vicky” had come to meet her, referring to her husband. Believing her husband was waiting outside, she walked towards the entrance.Footage shows him lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit punches her as she cries out for help, pulls out a knife in a flash and goes on a stabbing fit, puncturing her neck, abdomen and upper body several times as she slumps to the ground.School principal Tejpal is seen rushing into the corridor to rescue Sandhya after hearing her screams but is forced to step back as the attacker threatens him with the knife.“There were students inside the school and Sandhya was taking classes. He used her husband’s name to call her outside. No sooner did he reach the gate, he attacked her. He stabbed her over 20 times. When I tried to stop him, he threatened to attack me too. We rushed her to Al-Falah Medical College, where she was declared dead on arrival,” the principal told TOI.Police sources said Amit had allegedly bought the knife around two months ago and is suspected to have been planning the murder since then. While the exact number of stab wounds will be confirmed after the autopsy, CCTV footage showed him stabbing Sandhya about 20 times in just 13 seconds. Amit had come to the school on a motorcycle.Sandhya, who had a love marriage with Vikas, is survived by their two children — a five-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. The attack triggered panic on the campus. Teachers quickly moved frightened children back into classrooms while parents began arriving after news spread. Police cordoned off the school as forensic teams collected evidence.Based on a complaint by Sandhya’s husband, a case was registered under Section 103(1) (murder) of BNS at Sector 58 police station.Police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said the anti-vehicle theft squad and a team from Sikrona police station tracked down Amit within two hours.“During questioning, the accused said he knew Sandhya from the school in his village where she earlier taught. She later stopped speaking to him and warned of legal action if he continued following her,” Yadav added.Police said the accused will be produced before a local court and his custody sought for further interrogation. CCTV footage and other evidence are being examined as part of the probe, they added.
Article Summary: A stalker walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name. He then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent. The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village infaridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours.

Article Title: In MP village, kids risk lives every day, hop over dam pillars to reach school
Article Text:
Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the current education system in rural areas, like Kakraua, sufficient to support students? Yes, it meets their needs. No, it needs significant improvement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: Children from Kakraua village in MP's Vidisha district are forced to risk their lives every day by negotiating a precarious line of concrete pillars across a check dam on the Betwa river to reach their school - a route they take to avoid a much longer commute.A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media, raising fresh concerns about local infrastructure and student safety.Kakraua has a school only up to eighth grade.The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road. By crossing the check dam, the distance shrinks to roughly 1.5km, prompting nine students - five of them girls in the ninth grade - to use the risky shortcut daily.The village is part of the constituency of former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who is now the Union minister for agriculture.The dam-crossing involves walking across a series of exposed pillars that stand about three to four feet apart.Students hop about 10 pillars each trip. Villagers say the gap between pillars makes the route hazardous, especially during the monsoon when surfaces become slippery and the river's current increases."We have to work in the fields, so we can't drop our children off at school and back," said a parent."They find it easier to cross the dam nearby... We only have two options: we either stop sending our children to school or continue sending them this way even though it's dangerous."The consequences of skipping the unsafe route are already visible in the community.A student failed her final exams earlier this year after missing school because she could not cross the pillars due to her short height; she is repeating ninth grade this year.Parents fear that continued reliance on the shortcut could lead to further academic setbacks or, worse, an accident.District education officer N K Ahirwar acknowledged the problem. "I visited the spot and informed the collector about this," Ahirwar said."I have written to higher authorities to find a solution soon." However, he did not provide a timeline for the construction of a safe passage for river crossing.Local residents are now pressing authorities for an urgent solution to ensure uninterrupted schooling without endangering children's lives.
Article Summary: Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river to reach their school. A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media. The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road.

Article Title: 'Arrest Abhijeet Dipke immediately': Social media influencer files complaint against CJP founder
Article Text:
Ansari alleged that men associated with Abhijeet Dipke attacked him and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately.





NEW DELHI: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that men linked to the party attacked him in Maharashtra.Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately."Today, I have filed a written complaint against Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the CJP party, with the Delhi DCP, because I have proof that his men attacked me. I was attacked in Pune and in Aurangabad. There are already 2 cases filed on that, " Ansari told ANI.He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk during the recent protests, claiming the move prevented the law and order situation in the national capital from worsening."I want the Delhi police to immediately arrest Dipke. Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating. Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit, " Ansari added“Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating.Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit,” Ansari alleged.Earlier on Monday, Dipke had rejected comparisons between the CJP-led protests over alleged recruitment and examination irregularities and anti-government movements in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian protesters draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi's legacy of peaceful resistance.Dipke also spoke about the CJP's expansion plans, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and the state of education in India.Dipke also dismissed exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen's remarks comparing the CJP's protest in Delhi against exam irregularities with the 2024 movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government.“Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," he asserted.“We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us.“We don’t need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest,” Dipke said.People are drawing comparisons with the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because the alleged police brutality reminded them of scenes from those countries, he said.“The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.
Article Summary: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately. He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: Bankipur bypoll: Prashant Kishor adds a dash of yellow to Bihar palette of saffron & green
Article Text:
Jan Suraaj party workers celebrating Prashant Kishor's victory





PATNA: Bihar has been green. It has been saffron. Now Prashant Kishor brings yellow.Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP’s saffron and RJD’s green duopoly.Born in Rohtas in 1977, Kishor studied in Buxar, completed his Class XII from Patna Science College, earned a BBA from Lucknow University and a master’s in healthcare management from ASCI, Hyderabad. He did a French language course in France before spending eight years in a UN-supported public health programme.National prominence came after helping design PM Modi’s successful 2014 LS campaign. His organisation, I-PAC, went on to work with multiple political parties. He advised former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee and parties across Punjab, Andhra and Tamil Nadu, earning a reputation as one of the country’s most successful political consultants.After helping the Nitish-led Mahagathbandhan win in 2015, Kishor briefly joined JDU before returning to grassroots politics.A self-professed believer in Gandhi’s philosophy, he spent nearly two years on a padayatra across Bihar before launching Jan Suraaj Party on Oct 2, 2024. Its candidates drew a blank in the 2025 state polls, raising questions over whether his campaign skills could translate into votes.Barely eight months later, the answer arrived in Bankipur. Defeat would have dealt a crushing blow to both Kishor and Jan Suraaj. Instead, victory fuelled debate over whether Bihar has room for a third political force.“I did not contest to become an MLA or turn Bankipur into a metropolitan city like Bengaluru,” he said. “I wanted to send a message to BJP brass — generate employment, provide education and stop migration, or be prepared for similar results.”Married to Dr Jahnavi Das and father to a son, Kishor lives like a monk on campaign. He rarely watches TV news, hasn’t used a laptop in a decade, and relies only on his phone to stay connected with his grassroots network.
Article Summary: Prashant Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP's saffron and RJD's green duopoly.

Article Title: Supreme Court acquits man in jail for 22 years for wrong conviction
Article Text:
The high court had refused to hear him on the technical ground and prolonged his stay in jail by 10 more years

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A trial court’s failure to evaluate the evidence properly and the Odisha High Court remaining a mute spectator resulted in 22 years being erased from a person’s life as he was wrongly convicted and his appeal was not heard by the high court. Finally, the Supreme Court has come to his rescue and acquitted him.It is a classic case where a poor litigant’s fight for justice is frustrated at the altar of the judiciary itself, when the court refused hearing on technical grounds. The poor convict had already spent 12 years in jail when he approached the high court. The high court refused to hear him on the technical ground that there was a delay in filing an appeal, and it prolonged his stay in jail by 10 more years before he was acquitted by the Supreme Court, which had to admit that “access to justice still eludes the marginalised sections of our society and especially those convicted and imprisoned from among them”.“We are deeply dismayed, and equally perturbed by the order which rejected an application seeking condonation of delay of 3,157 days and as a consequence dismissed the ‘Jail Memo of Appeal’ against the order of conviction under Section 302, with sentence imposed of life imprisonment where the convict had, at the time of the impugned order suffered incarceration of 12 years and now a further period of 10 years; a total of 22 years,” a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said.It said the high court ought to have also considered that it was an appeal through jail and the court ought to have taken a practical view, or rather a sympathetic view, of the matter and at least ought to have condoned the delay to give one opportunity to the petitioner to argue his criminal appeal on the merits.“When the three pillars of democracy consistently endeavour to bring legal aid to the doorsteps of every citizen, especially the poor...we...should sensitise ourselves in taking a liberal approach...Not a mere liberal approach but a pro-active one to condone delay, however large it is, when a convict knocks at the door of a Court...which in the present case raises some real concerns,” the bench said.Examining the evidence, the court concluded that it was not a fit case of conviction on the basis of a sole eyewitness, which was not reliable and was shaky. It acquitted him in a triple murder case.“... a person taken into custody on mere suspicion from whom a confession, though not admissible, was extracted employing third-degree methods, the trial court fails to evaluate the evidence properly, and the high court remains a mute spectator...resulting in 22 years being erased out of a person’s life without any reliable evidence,” the court said.
Article Summary: The high court refused to hear him on the technical ground that there was a delay in filing an appeal. The trial court’s failure to evaluate the evidence properly resulted in 22 years being erased from a person's life as he was wrongly convicted. Finally, the Supreme Court has come to his rescue and acquitted him.

Article Title: Meta apologises for ‘error in restricting PM’s video’
Article Text:
The government says that the company admits lapses on child porn, deepfakes

Officials told Meta it could lose safe harbour status

NEW DELHI: Amid mounting scrutiny, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has apologised to the government for Facebook taking down PM Modi’s video, and the social media giant’s lapses related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM), deepfake content and errors in operating its platforms, government officials said. The tech major also confirmed that it took money to boost certain types of content, the officials added.Meta blamed technical glitches for Modi’s video being taken down, in which he had reached out to student protesters.“I apologised to the minister (Ashwini Vaishnaw) on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post,” Meta’s chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan said in a statement. Government officials said Zuckerberg’s apology was communicated through Kaplan.The apology came hours after Zuckerberg was given a three-day ultimatum by a parliamentary standing committee headed by BJP’s Nishikant Dubey on Wednesday to either apologise for taking down PM Modi’s video or lose the ‘safe harbour’ that protects Meta from any liability for the content posted on its platforms.The social media giant acknowledged during discussions with the government that significant sums had been paid for boosting certain categories of content and accepted that paid promotion had resulted in illegal content being amplified for specific audiences, officials said.The company expressed regret over the lapses and admitted mistakes in the way the platform had been operating, officials added.The meeting happened against the backdrop of widespread indignation in BJP and government quarters that Facebook facilitated algorithmic manipulation to fan discontent against the government over paper leaks and promote content, including a barrage of vile reels targeting the PM. Meta representatives will be summoned again, officials said, without disclosing the purpose or scope of the next meeting.Meta apologised for the shortcomings and assured authorities that corrective steps would be taken.Authorities also conveyed to Meta that it could not automatically claim protection available to intermediaries under Indian law if it actively selected who received content through algorithmic amplification or paid promotion. The company was told that such conduct could place it outside the definition of an intermediary, rendering it vulnerable to action by authorities and lawsuits by individuals.The government also sought details of safeguards to prevent the dissemination of CSAM, deepfakes and other harmful material. Officials said Meta accepted that illegal content had been promoted and acknowledged shortcomings in its systems.The government, meanwhile, is examining global regulatory approaches to children’s online safety as part of a broader review of its policy and legal framework. International models for protecting children online are being studied to assess whether additional safeguards or legislative changes are required as digital platforms come under increasing scrutiny over harmful and illegal content, it said in a statement.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg has apologised to the government for Facebook taking down PM Modi’s video. The social media giant also admitted lapses related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and deepfake content. The tech major also confirmed that it took money to boost certain types of content.

Article Title: Decide on raising retirement age of judges by Sept 2: SC to states
Article Text:
The Supreme Court requested high courts to pass appropriate full-court resolutions in favour of increasing the age of superannuation of judicial officers from 60 to 62 years

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Attempting to bring judicial officers’ retirement age on a par with that for HC judges, the Supreme Court on Wednesday asked states to decide by Sept 2 on increasing the superannuation age of trial court judges from 60 to 62 years while brushing aside pleas of financial constraints and the disparity it would create vis-a-vis government employees.In the early 1990s, the Supreme Court had increased through a judgment the retirement age of judicial officers across India from 58 to 60 years. This time, however, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that instead of a judicial ruling, it would be better if state governments made the decision on their own. The strength of trial court judges has doubled since 1992, from around 10,000 to over 20,000 at present. The number of HC judges has increased from 568 in 1992 to 1,114 now.A few states have increased the age of retirement for judicial officers from 60 to 61, akin to similar benefits for government employees. Some states argued that increasing the age of superannuation of judicial officers to 62 years would create disparity and cause discontent among government employees, who too would demand identical benefits, entailing a huge financial burden for the government.But the bench rejected both these objections. It said that when a judicial officer retires, the government pays them a lump-sum amount and pension, which is more than half of their last-drawn salary. On filling the vacancy, the government pays a salary to the new appointee. Retaining experienced and seasoned judicial officers would be financially beneficial for the state and judiciary, it said.Rejecting the argument of parity with government employees, the CJI-led bench said judicial officers are appointed by the government under a constitutional scheme and hence form a class separate from that of government employees. “Both the reasons given by states are untenable. But we are of the opinion that the issue can be resolved amicably by administrative decisions of states,” the bench said.Asking advocates general of states to persuade their respective governments, the bench said, “States must revisit the issue of enhancing the retirement age of judicial officers irrespective of the present retirement age of government employees.”The Supreme Court requested high courts to strengthen the hands of state governments on the issue by passing appropriate full-court resolutions in favour of increasing the age of superannuation of judicial officers from 60 to 62 years.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court asked states to decide by Sept 2 on increasing the superannuation age of trial court judges from 60 to 62 years. The Supreme Court had increased through a judgment the retirement age of judicial officers across India from 58 to 60 years in the early 1990s.

Article Title: Rijiju reaches out to Rahul on delimitation bill

NEW DELHI: The government on Wednesday revived its bid to secure Parliament’s nod for its ambitious delimitation legislation that proposes to raise Lok Sabha’s strength by over 50% and implement one-third reservation for women from 2029, and appeared keen to press ahead despite LoP Rahul Gandhi rejecting its outreach for support.Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju raised the issue during his nearly 50-minute meeting with Rahul, who reiterated the Opposition’s stand that the proposed move would allow the government to redraw Lok Sabha constituencies to the NDA’s advantage in the next elections.The meeting was part of the government’s outreach to break the Parliament impasse, which has seen little business due to protests over multiple issues. However, speculation grew that the government may revive the Constitution amendment bill that was defeated in the last session.The timing remains uncertain. While a government functionary said it could be introduced before Aug 13, when the session is scheduled to end, official sources indicated Parliament may be reconvened after Aug 15 instead of being prorogued.There are indications that the government will push the Foreign Contributions Regulation (Amendment) Bill, criticised by Opposition parties, NGOs, Muslim organisations and church bodies.On Tuesday, several of these groups sought the support of US lawmaker Riley Moore.At Wednesday’s meeting, Rahul Gandhi was accompanied by AICC general secretary KC Venugopal and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. According to sources, Congress conveyed that the rationale behind both the legislations was flawed.Venugopal said, “Minister Kiren Rijiju came to discuss delimitation and asked whether the Opposition’s stand had changed. We said we stick to the stand we took in the budget session... It has not changed.”Asked about the FCRA amendment bill, Venugopal said, “We will not allow the government to pass such a draconian bill.”On speculation that Rijiju hinted at a special session for the delimitation bill, Congress sources said he made no such suggestion. During the previous session too, the government had reconvened Parliament for three days after the scheduled end by not proroguing it. Having suffered the embarrassment of the earlier bill being defeated after securing only 298 votes against the required 352, the government appears to have strengthened its numbers for another attempt.Its position has improved since then as 26 Opposition MPs from Mamata Banerjee-led TMC and Sena UBT have joined the NDA, while DMK’s ties with Congress have deteriorated after the latter aligned with Vijay-led TVK in Tamil Nadu.The possibility of DMK, which had strongly opposed the bill earlier, extending support has increased after the party indicated it could back the proposal if southern states’ interests are protected. To allay such concerns, home minister Amit Shah had assured LS during the earlier debate that every state’s seats would increase by 50%, preserving their existing share in the House.There is a view that the government may incorporate the home minister’s assurance into the bill to win over parties such as DMK. NCP (SP) has also said a proposal guaranteeing the same increase in seats for every state should not pose a problem.
Article Summary: The government appears keen to press ahead despite LoP Rahul Gandhi rejecting its outreach for support. Speculation grew that the government may revive the Constitution amendment bill that was defeated in the last session. There are indications the government will push the Foreign Contributions Regulation (Amendment) Bill.

Article Title: Government hits out at Pakistan’s malicious propaganda against India

Such state-sponsored violence against unarmed civilians exposes the profound hypocrisy of the Pakistani establishment,” he said.“Instead of engaging in predictable diplomatic theatre, Pakistan would be well-advised to stop the bloodshed in PoJK, take credible, verifiable, and irreversible action against terror networks operating from its soil, and immediately vacate all Indian territories under its illegal and forcible occupation. Article Title: Congress vs Congress in Punjab: With 'sleeper cell' warning, party puts Channi camp on notice
Article Text:
Baghel and Warring warned of action against "sleeper cells" amid Congress's escalating feud with former CM Channi

Congress message for Charanjit Singh Channi?

Channi from 'chosen one' to ‘dissident’

Why Congress is backing Warring

So, what should be the way forward?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Will the Congress crack the whip against dissidents in Punjab? With differences between state president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi becoming an embarrassing public spectacle, the Congress has sent out a strong message to disgruntled leaders in Punjab, warning of action against "sleeper cells" within its own ranks in the poll-bound state."We have to identify and fight the sleeper cells inside the Congress. A strong organisation at the booth level is the key to victory," said AICC general secretary and Punjab in-charge Bhupesh Baghel, in a clear message to those who have raised a banner of revolt against the leadership. Baghel declared that the Congress was fighting a "multi-cornered battle" not only against political rivals but also against those within the party allegedly working for opponents.Taking forward Baghel’s message, state Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring declared that no party ticket would be given to anyone found operating as part of "sleeper cells." "While the high command will decide the candidates, I will ensure that no person working against the party gets a ticket. Loyalty to the Congress is non-negotiable," the Punjab Congress chief asserted.Warring also targeted former state Congress chief Sunil Jakhar, who is now with the BJP, accusing him of betraying the Congress during the 2022 assembly elections.Warring alleged that Jakhar had worked in tacit understanding with the BJP despite heading the Congress campaign committee.While Baghel and Warring did not take any names, their target was obvious. The dissidents in Punjab are backing former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, who has been unhappy after being denied the post of state Congress chief in the organisational reshuffle that was announced on July 1. The move triggered a storm that continues to rock and embarrass the party even a month later.With Warring retained as state Congress chief by the party high command, Channi and his supporters have missed no opportunity to show their “dissent” and openly challenge the party’s decision. Even the presence of Baghel in the state has not helped to ease tempers. From poster war to sloganeering at party meetings - here’s how the open show of defiance has played out.While "Go Back Baghel" poster surfaced in Muktsar, another poster surfaced in Ferozepur showing Channi wearing a vest with "RSS" printed on it.Supporters of Channi have indulged in sloganeering at party programmes attended by Warring and Bhupesh Baghel in Patiala and Sangrur.In another event in Sangrur town, activists of both camps clashed in the presence of senior leaders.Channi's camp, comprising several state leaders, has been demanding the replacement of Warring by citing specific instances on how the state chief had created divisions within the party leadership.Last month, they even gave an open ultimatum to the central leadership to make Channi, the Congress MP from Jalandhar and a prominent Dalit face, as state chief saying that under Warring's leadership the Congress cannot come to power.Interestingly in 2022, Channi was the chosen one as the Congress grappled with intense internal fighting between the then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh and his challenger Navjot Singh Sidhu.With the two senior leaders engaging in open power tussle, Congress sidelined both and picked Channi to lead the state and the party in the 2022 assembly elections. But under Channi, the Congress was decimated and reduced to 18 seats from the 77 it had won in 2017 under Captain Amarinder Singh.Channi, who has now been made the head of the Congress campaign committee, has dropped enough hints that he does not accept the leadership of Warring.And that brings us to the present Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who was handed over the reins of the party by Rahul Gandhi in 2022 after the humiliating defeat in assembly elections.Warring, who has faced sloganeering from supporters of Channi during recent party programmes, has refused to step down. He has said that if the party high command decides to replace him, he would continue to work to strengthen the organisation."I have no desire to be the chief minister. I will better retire than leave the Congress. Rahul Gandhi also knows that Raja Warring can die, but never compromise with the BJP," he said in one of his speeches.Warring has cited Congress’s 2024 Lok Sabha performance - when it won seven of 13 seats - to justify his efforts at reviving the party.In a highly emotional speech at his hometown in Muktsar recently, Warring had said: "Everyone is after my life. Akalis, BJP and the broom (AAP) and even some of our own are after me. I have not committed any sin and my only sin is that when we came from 80 to 18 I was handed over the reins of the party."Maintaining that he started from the scratch when the morale of the party's rank and file was low and some leaders preferred to stay abroad for months together, Warring said he led from the front.Warring played down the slogans raised by Channi's supporters during party events and said, "People oppose those who are successful. Those 20-25 poor souls who come, one doesn't even know how they are brought in or what they are told. I actually feel sorry for them; this sort of thing has been happening for ages. The event went well; people listened to the speeches, and there was a huge crowd. People do these things; it doesn't matter. I have been in politics for 25 years."Former Punjab minister Razia Sultana called upon the party high command to take strict action against all those who were indulging in indiscipline and damaging the party. She warned that if timely action was not taken, the party could suffer major damage."Nip the evil in the bud," Sultana remarked.But can the Congress do that? Theoretically yes, but practically we haven’t seen the grand-old-party take clear leadership decisions, except perhaps in Karnataka. For the Congress high command, the standard playbook for handling leadership tussles in states has been “ambiguity is the best policy.”And Punjab has been no different. One can only hope that the Congress acts before it is too late. The strong warning to dissidents is a welcome first step, but it remains to be seen if the party high command can follow this up with action without being scared of the consequences.
Article Summary: Congress warns of action against "sleeper cells" amid feud with former CM Channi. State president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi are locked in power tussle. Supporters of Channi have indulged in sloganeering at party programmes.

Article Title: ‘Miles to go before I sleep’: Omar gets poetic, says ‘wounds of Art 370 abrogation yet to heal’
Article Text:

JAMMU: A row erupted after PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti was seen holding the Tricolour upside down during a candlelight protest over Article 370 on Tuesday evening. CM Omar Abdullah, however, played it down, saying he believed it was an inadvertent mistake rather than a deliberate act.“I cannot believe that a person who served as a CM would deliberately display the flag of the country upside down. It must be a mistake,” he said.

SRINAGAR/JAMMU: Striking a poetic note on the seventh anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370 and bifurcation of the state of Jammu & Kashmir into two Union Territories, chief minister Omar Abdullah invoked celebrated American poet Robert Lee Frost as he said the wounds caused by the move had still not healed, and vowed that “the injustices done to us will be corrected”.“7 years, we haven’t forgotten & we haven’t reconciled far less accepted our current circumstances. The PDP march was led by Iltija Mufti, who accused cops of manhandling her during Tuesday’s attempted protest.“It’s on this day we were caged like animals while a govt drunk on power stripped our state of its special status, flag, residuary powers and constitution. Our peaceful fight for it will continue till the day we get every bit of it back,” Iltija said.Lt governor Manoj Sinha, on the other hand, hailed the decision, saying it had “dismantled the terror ecosystem to a large extent, strengthened law and order, restored equal rights and created opportunities that allow families to rebuild their lives with confidence”. “The transformation we witness today in J&K is due to the historic changes of Aug 5, 2019. That day marked a constitutional correction and a new beginning for the UT,” he said.

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Wednesday passed the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill — replacing a British-era law — without discussion amid opposition protests and sloganeering on multiple issues, as members refused to heed the chair’s call to debate the legislation.The government accused the opposition of disrupting proceedings. Article Title: ‘Criminal cases can’t have lifespan of turtle’: Supreme Court on activist’s trial delay

Supreme Court of India

NEW DELHI: “Lifespan of a criminal trial cannot be that of a turtle,” SC said Wednesday, taking exception to the over-three-year-long trial of an activist of the outlawed Popular Front of India (PFI) facing charges that entail a maximum five-year jail term, with no prospect of its early end because of 700 prosecution witnesses lined up against him.Petitioner Shahid Khan , who was arrested on Sept 22, 2022, has appealed against a Karnataka HC order rejecting his bail plea. Turning to Karnataka counsel, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Don’t make a mockery of the trial. ”

NEW DELHI: Meta officials apologised to the IT minister for removing PM Modi's video while Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg also reportedly sent his apologies to the central government on Wednesday for CSAM (child sexual abuse material), deepfake content, and errors in operating the platform."I apologised to the minister on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post," said Joel Kaplan, chief global affairs officer at Meta, as quoted by ANI. Kaplan, with his team, had met Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Wednesday.The government flagged the removal of content posted by verified accounts belonging to prominent personalities after a video of PM Modi was briefly removed from Facebook. The video, in which PM Modi addressed students and Gen Z on examination controversies and action against paper leaks, was removed from Facebook for around five to six hours before being restored.Separately, the IT also giant admitted that they were paid a "lot of money" for boosting certain type of content to "specific audiences", as per PTI sources. The sources also said that Meta was told that its eligibility for safe-harbour protection under the IT Act could be questioned, as its platforms actively select and distribute content to users rather than merely hosting third-party content. Under Section 79, safe-harbour protection is subject to conditions on how an intermediary handles and distributes such content.The development comes as senior Meta executives met government officials to discuss compliance with Indian laws, content moderation, child sexual CSAM and safeguards around AI-generated content.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Meta executives, including Joel Kaplan, the company's head of public policy, met government officials on Wednesday and are set to meet again on Thursday.Krishnan said the government wants Meta to explain what measures it has taken to tackle CSAM on its platforms and how effectively it is monitoring synthetically generated content. “We want to ensure that compliance happens. There are a range of issues,” Krishnan said.He added that the government wants to understand the measures being taken to address CSAM and the extent to which AI-generated content is being monitored.The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Electronics and Information Technology had taken a “very serious” view of the incident and warned that Meta could lose its safe-harbour protection under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act if Zuckerberg failed to apologise within three days last week.Krishnan said such takedowns should be backed by stronger safeguards, particularly when they involve accounts of prominent public figures.

Article Title: Air India turbulence scare: After the drop, the trauma lingers
Article Text:
Doctors say the physical and mental toll can last for months (Photo: ANI).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi that suddenly dropped nearly 300 feet after encountering severe turbulence on Tuesday has once again highlighted that the impact of such incidents extends well beyond visible injuries. While at least 14 passengers and cabin crew members were injured and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has launched an investigation, doctors say the physical and psychological consequences of severe turbulence can linger for days, weeks or even months.Psychiatrists warn that even passengers who escape with minor or no physical injuries may develop significant psychological distress. "The sudden perception of imminent danger, combined with the loss of control and visible panic, can activate the body's survival response," said Dr Rajesh Sagar, professor in the Department of Psychiatry at AIIMS.Dr Sagar said that passengers may experience persistent fear, anxiety, sleep disturbances, intrusive memories and heightened alertness after the incident. In some cases, the experience can trigger Acute Stress Disorder (ASD) within days, which may progress to Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) if symptoms persist beyond a month."The psychological impact should not be underestimated simply because there are no major physical injuries," Dr Sagar said.He advised passengers to seek help if they continue to experience nightmares, flashbacks, avoidance of flying or emotional distress. Early psychological support based on the principles of Psychological First Aid can reduce the risk of long-term trauma, he added.Doctors also cautioned against dismissing apparently minor physical injuries sustained during turbulence. Dr (Maj.) Mukesh Garg, Director of Orthopaedics, Arthroscopy and Sports Injury at Sarvodaya Hospital, said passengers thrown against seats, overhead bins or cabin interiors may sustain bruises, ligament injuries, fractures or injuries to the neck and spine."Not all injuries become obvious immediately," he said. "Soft tissue injuries, ligament tears and mild concussions may take several hours to become apparent. Pain, swelling and stiffness often worsen over the next 24 to 48 hours."He advised anyone who suffered a blow to the head, neck or back to undergo medical evaluation even if symptoms initially appear mild. Warning signs requiring immediate medical attention include severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, dizziness, confusion, blurred vision, weakness or numbness of the limbs, difficulty walking, severe neck pain and loss of bladder or bowel control.Experts also recommend that passengers who develop a fear of flying after severe turbulence gradually rebuild confidence through counselling, breathing exercises and relaxation techniques. Starting with shorter flights, travelling with a trusted companion and keeping the seatbelt fastened throughout the journey can also help restore a sense of safety and control.
Article Summary: Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi suddenly dropped nearly 300 feet after severe turbulence on Tuesday. At least 14 passengers and cabin crew members were injured and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation has launched an investigation. Doctors say the physical and psychological consequences of severe turbulence can linger for days, weeks or even months.

NEW DELHI: Network slicing, which enables telecom service providers to provide different speeds of internet to different categories of consumers, could soon become a reality in India. Following a request from some large operators, the telecom department had asked Trai to examine this, and on Wednesday, the regulator issued a draft quality of service norms that factor in this controversial technology that some fear may affect net neutrality.The draft amendments to the Standards of Quality of Service of Access (Wireline and Wireless) and Broadband (Wireline and Wireless) Service Regulations, 2024, say: “...service provider must ensure that sufficient capacity is available in the network and shall submit the details, as per the format and manner prescribed by the authority, before launch of such network slicing.”The draft proposes to change the “typical download and upload speed offered to the subscribers” sentence in the existing rule with “technology-wise typical download and upload speed offered to subscribers for each tariff offering.” If cleared, telecom operators will be able to charge differently for different services like 4G and 5G, unlike now when both services have the same charge.

Article Title: Navigation sat NVS-03 ready for launch, 3 more satellites to follow: Space min Jitendra Singh in LS
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The government is working to have the country’s Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System or NaVIC up and running again as it plans to launch four satellites in the near future.“NVS-03 is ready for launch after incorporation of all corrective measures arising from the NVS-02 anomaly. It will be followed by the launch of NVS-04 and NVS-05. One more satellite is planned thereafter to complete the seven-satellite NavIC base layer constellation,” space minister Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in Lok Sabha on Wednesday.He, however, did not mention the timeline for these launches.Noting the failure of replacement satellite NVS-02 in 2025, Jitendra Singh said, “Necessary corrective measures have been incorporated and successfully implemented and tested in CMS-03 satellite. The same will be followed in subsequent satellites, including the NavIC series of satellites carrying bi-propellant systems.”Currently, only IRNSS 1-B, IRNSS 1-L and NVS-01 are capable of providing navigation services. But for the NaVIC system to be operational effectively, at least four satellites with operational atomic clocks are required. So, NavIC is no longer providing standalone positioning services.In March this year, the last atomic clock on board Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System-1F (IRNSS-1F) stopped functioning, paralysing NavIC.The first-generation satellites for NavIC were launched between 2013 and 2018. However, the constellation of satellites soon began to face issues, with the atomic clocks on board several IRNSS series satellites repeatedly malfunctioning.The NVS series represents the second-generation satellites for NavIC. While Isro successfully placed NVS-01 in the desired orbit in 2023, the 2025 launch of NVS-02 failed. This has delayed the launch of NVS-03, NVS-04 and NVS-05.
Article Summary: The government is working to have the country’s Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System or NaVIC up and running again. It plans to launch four satellites in the near future. Currently, only IRNSS 1-B, IRN SS 1-L and NVS-01 are capable of providing navigation services.

NEW DELHI: Bihar minister Deepak Prakash was on Tuesday nominated to the state Legislative Council, days after the Supreme Court questioned his continuance in the cabinet without being a legislator.According to a gazette notification, governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd.) nominated Prakash to the vacant seat left by BJP MLC Devesh Kumar's resignation.Prakash was first inducted into the then Nitish Kumar-led Bihar cabinet in November last year and was recently re-inducted into the BJP-led government headed by Samrat Choudhary. On both occasions, he was not a member of either House of the state legislature.His father, Upendra Kushwaha, whose Rashtriya Lok Morcha is a constituent of the BJP-led ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), thanked the BJP leadership but insisted the nomination was unrelated to the court proceedings.“I express my gratitude towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin. We shall work to take Bihar forward," Kushwaha told reporters, according to PTI."People file petitions for all sorts of things. When Deepak Prakash had first become a minister, the NDA had in principle decided that he would be sent to the Legislative Council in due course," he added.BJP sources, however, admitted Kumar had "sacrificed" his seat to accommodate Prakash. Kumar, whose tenure had less than a year left, resigned on July 31, saying it was a "voluntary decision".Last week, while hearing a petition challenging Prakash's continuance as minister, the Supreme Court raised the "legal question" of "how long can you have an unelected minister".Under constitutional rules, a person appointed as a minister must become a member of either House of the legislature within six months.

The Biju Janata Dal (BJD) on Wednesday opposed the proposed setting up of a nuclear power plant in Odisha, alleging that the BJP government was putting public safety at risk to benefit private companies. The party also warned of a statewide agitation if the project moved forward.The criticism came days after a representative of a private company met Odisha deputy chief minister KV Singh Deo, who also holds the state's energy portfolio. According to the BJD, the company has proposed establishing a 3,000 MW nuclear power plant in Odisha.Addressing a press conference, BJD senior general secretary Lekhashree Samantsinghar claimed that a nuclear power plant would pose a serious threat to the health and safety of people living in the state.She accused the BJP's "double-engine government" of ignoring public welfare in favour of corporate interests."Whenever the subject of nuclear or atomic energy arises, it naturally creates fear in people's minds. In 1945, the nuclear bombings reduced the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki to ruins. In 1986, the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant suffered a catastrophic explosion, and in 2011, a similar disaster occurred at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Plant," she said.Samantsinghar added that the consequences of those disasters were still being felt and argued that nuclear power carries significant risks to human life.She further claimed that nuclear energy has traditionally remained under government control in most countries because of its strategic importance. However, she alleged that the BJP government was now changing that approach by opening the sector to private companies."However, under the BJP government, this long-standing principle is being altered by transferring nuclear energy into the hands of private companies. For its own interests, the BJP government is showing complete disregard for the lives and safety of the people of Odisha," she alleged.The BJD leader also questioned the Centre's decision to amend rules governing the nuclear sector. She claimed that Parliament passed legislation in December 2025 allowing greater private participation, following which private companies began exploring projects in Odisha.According to Samantsinghar, India currently has about 8.8 GW of government-owned nuclear power capacity, and increasing it to 100 GW by involving private players would be unsafe. She argued that sectors linked to national security should remain under government control.The opposition party also alleged that the Odisha government was acting on directions from the Centre rather than taking independent decisions."Since the formation of the BJP government in Odisha, the state government has been functioning under the directions of the Centre and is unable to take any independent decisions without instructions from Delhi. Acting on the directions of the central government, the state is determined to establish a nuclear power plant in Odisha by compromising the interests of the people," she alleged.The BJD urged the state government to abandon the proposal, warning that it would launch a mass movement if the project went ahead."Otherwise, the Biju Janata Dal would launch a mass agitation to safeguard the interests of the people of the State," she told reporters. The Odisha government had not responded to the allegations at the time of filing the report.
