NEW DELHI: Parliament remained paralysed for the 13th consecutive day on Wednesday as relentless protests by Opposition parties forced repeated adjournments in both Houses, even as the government pushed through key legislative business.Amid the deadlock, efforts to break the impasse gathered pace with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju holding meetings with Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and Union home minister Amit Shah , while Prime Minister Narendra Modi separately met BJP MPs over breakfast.Opposition MPs led by Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra marched from Prerna Sthal to Makar Dwar, demanding accountability from Amit Shah over the alleged police action against CJP protesters on July 20.They also raised the alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement issue and other matters. Priyanka Gandhi said those responsible for ordering the alleged use of pellet guns, tear gas and lathi charges against students must be held accountable, asserting that "This is a democracy, not a dictatorship; it is not someone's royal court."Rijiju dismissed speculation that the Monsoon Session could be extended or that a special session might be convened later this month.He said there was no proposal before the government to either prolong the current session or hold a separate sitting in mid-August.His clarification came amid continued disruptions that have prevented the Lok Sabha from completing Question Hour since the session began on July 20.Despite the logjam, the Lok Sabha passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, by voice vote without discussion after Opposition members refused to end their protest.Rijiju accused Opposition parties of deliberately stalling the House despite time being allotted for debate. He also criticised the Congress, CPI and Samajwadi Party over their protests relating to the alleged Ram Temple donation theft, alleging they had disrespected Lord Ram through demonstrations inside the Parliament complex.In a significant political development, Rijiju met Rahul Gandhi in his Parliament office for nearly 50 minutes in what sources described as a confidence-building exercise aimed at ending the parliamentary deadlock. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was present throughout the meeting, while Gaurav Gogoi and K C Venugopal joined later.According to sources, discussions covered the proposed Delimitation Bill, the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) Bill and other contentious issues that have fuelled the ongoing standoff. It was Rijiju's second meeting with Rahul Gandhi in the past 10 days, signalling continued backchannel engagement between the government and the Opposition despite the public confrontation inside Parliament.Soon after meeting Rahul Gandhi, Rijiju met Amit Shah at Parliament House. Sources said the government is preparing to engage the Opposition on the proposed FCRA Bill and Shah is expected to address the issue in Parliament.Rijiju is also expected to reach out to leaders of other Opposition parties, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, in an effort to build consensus and restore normal functioning of the House. The proposed FCRA amendments have emerged as one of the key flashpoints of the session alongside the protests over NEET, police action against students and the Ram Temple donation controversy.Trinamool Congress leader Derek O'Brien accused the government of being responsible for the continued disruption in Parliament, alleging that Amit Shah's prolonged absence from the House had worsened the situation. O'Brien maintained that Opposition MPs continued to perform their parliamentary duties despite the protests by raising public issues through Zero Hour notices and starred questions.He highlighted his own notices seeking national recognition of the 75th anniversary of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity and raising concerns over the proposed FCRA Bill. TMC sources said the party had submitted more than 100 questions during the session on issues ranging from MGNREGA dues and manual scavenging to air pollution, bank frauds, the UDAN scheme and the Nirbhaya Fund.Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a breakfast meeting with 37 BJP MPs at his official residence as part of his regular outreach during Parliament sessions. The gathering included MPs associated with the NDA as well as former AAP leaders who later joined the BJP. Senior BJP leaders Tarun Chugh, Vinod Tawde and party chief Nitin Nabin also attended.Sources told news agency PTI said the Prime Minister shared personal experiences and discussed governance, parliamentary strategy and constituency feedback with the MPs. The interaction forms part of Modi's practice of meeting smaller groups of BJP parliamentarians during every session to strengthen coordination and receive direct feedback from lawmakers.Despite the disruptions, the Rajya Sabha passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, completing Parliament's approval of the legislation. The Bill raises the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.Replying to the debate, law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said the increase was a "demand of the time" given the growing workload, rising pendency and the need for more Constitution Benches.He said the expansion would improve disposal rates and help ensure quicker access to justice. Meghwal also highlighted the government's ongoing investment in expanding Supreme Court infrastructure and reiterated its commitment to judicial reforms and the independence of the judiciary.
Article Summary: Parliament remained paralysed for the 13th consecutive day on Wednesday as relentless protests by Opposition parties forced repeated adjournments in both Houses. Despite the logjam, the Lok Sabha passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, by voice vote without discussion. Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a breakfast meeting with 37 BJP MPs at his official residence.

Article Title: 'No special session of Parliament': Govt on Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills
Article Text:

The government on Wednesday rejected media reports claiming that Parliament would convene a three-day special session from August 16 to 18 to consider the Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills."No proposal to extend the dates of the Parliament session and no special session from August 16 to 18 on Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills," Union minister Kiren Rijiju told ANI.The Monsoon Session of Parliament commenced on July 20 and will conclude on August 13.Rijiju's announcement came on a day when he reportedly held a one-on-one meeting with Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in an effort to break the ongoing Parliament deadlock.During the meeting, which lasted around 50 minutes, Rijiju is said to have discussed the possible reintroduction of the Delimitation and Women's Reservation Bills. However, Rahul Gandhi is not believed to have given any commitment on the proposals.Opposition parties in both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha have been demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah over the Delhi Police's alleged use of force against student protesters during their march to Parliament on July 20, the opening day of the Monsoon Session. As Delhi is a Union territory, the Delhi Police functions under the Union home ministry.While Shah is yet to respond, leading to the current logjam, he s expected to speak in Parliament when the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, is introduced in for discussion and passage.
Article Summary: The Monsoon Session of Parliament commenced on July 20 and will conclude on August 13. Union minister Kiren Rijiju reportedly held a one-on-one meeting with Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in an effort to break the ongoing Parliament deadlock. Opposition parties in both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha have been demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah.

Article Title: 'Don't use students for politics': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi over Jantar Mantar protest claims
Article Text:

BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of pushing 'false narrative'

BJP questions Rahul Gandhi's silence on Jharkhand students

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Wednesday hit back at Congress leader and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of police excesses during the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' student protest, accusing him of spreading a "false narrative" and using students for political purposes.Addressing a press conference, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra rejected the Congress MP's claim that security forces fired on protesters, reiterating the party's stand that "no bullets were fired" during the demonstration."A short while ago, Rahul Gandhi addressed a press conference along with some of the young people who participated in the protest in Delhi on the 20th. I want to make one thing very clear. What I am saying today is meant for Rahul Gandhi, not for those young people. They are our children, they belong to the nation and they are the country's future," Patra said."We had clearly stated earlier that no firing took place during the 'Sansad Chalo' protest in Delhi on the 20th. I am repeating it today with the same sense of responsibility because this is a sensitive issue. We do not want misinformation to spread or falsehoods to be accepted as facts. Therefore, I want to state once again, calmly and clearly, that no bullets were fired during the 'Sansad Chalo' protest in Delhi on the 20th," he added.Patra alleged that Rahul was attempting to use students to advance a political narrative and said the BJP's criticism was directed only at the Congress leader."One should never attempt to play politics by using innocent children, resting a gun on their shoulders, as Rahul Gandhi is doing. Children are the future of our country; they are not at fault," he said."We want to expose the false narrative and the 'bunch of lies' that Rahul Gandhi is trying to propagate. The country's children should remain fearless," he added.Responding to allegations raised by some student protesters during the former Congress President's press conference, Patra said students should not be divided on religious lines."I also heard Muskan say today, 'I am Muskan Sharma.' Muskan, whether you are Muskan Sharma or Muskan Khan, you are a daughter of this country. Whether your surname is Sharma or Khan, you belong to India. This country progresses through the spirit of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Vikas'. Rahul Gandhi's attempt to push a divisive agenda is completely wrong," he said.The BJP spokesperson also accused Rae Bareli MP of adopting a selective approach by focusing only on one set of protesting students while ignoring others."The children of Jharkhand are children too. They, too, are protesting. Rahul Gandhi should interact with some of the children from Jharkhand as well. He should understand their pain and suffering. Why isn't he visiting Jharkhand?" Patra asked.He also rejected Rahul's allegation that Union home minister Amit Shah was avoiding Parliament over the issue."Rahul Gandhi's statement that Amit Shah is not coming to the House... Rahul ji, are you even allowing the House to function? Such an uproar is created by Rahul Gandhi and his MPs that the House has to be adjourned within two minutes. The minister in charge of the department under discussion always attends. When the Home Minister's department is discussed, he will certainly be present," Patra said.He further accused the Congress leader of disrupting Parliament while simultaneously alleging that ministers were not responding."The House begins its proceedings at 11 am, but Rahul Gandhi and his MPs create such a ruckus that it has to be adjourned within minutes. When the House reconvenes, they again reach the Speaker's desk, raise slogans and wave placards so they can be seen on television. In such a situation, how can they expect Parliament to function?" he said.Earlier in the day, Rahul Gandhi met student protesters who had participated in demonstrations against alleged irregularities in the NEET examinations and accused the Centre of trying to suppress democratic dissent.He said that a 15-year-old girl had been forced to apologise and claimed students were assaulted during the July 20 protest.Targeting Union home minister Amit Shah, Rahul alleged that Shah was responsible for the alleged violence against protesters."The person who is responsible for this violence... is Amit Shah. He does not have the decency to come to Parliament. Either he did not know that this violence was being carried out on the children, in which case he is incompetent, or he ordered the shooting of the pellet gun and the violence on these children. It means he is culpable. Either way, he is responsible," Rahul had said.Several students who appeared alongside Congress leader also alleged police brutality, including claims of pellet injuries, baton charges and harassment during the July 20 protest.The BJP has denied those allegations and maintained that no firing took place during the demonstration.
Article Summary: BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of police excesses during the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' student protest. Spokesman Sambit Patra accuses Rahul of spreading a "false narrative" and using students for political purposes. Patra also rejects Rahul's allegation that Union home minister Amit Shah was avoiding Parliament over the issue.

Article Title: IMA threatens nationwide strike over Maharashtra move to register CCMP-trained Homeopaths
Article Text:
IMA Headquarters termed the government’s August 3 Government Resolution (GR) “illegal”.

NEW DELHI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has threatened a nationwide strike if the Maharashtra government does not withdraw its recent decision permitting registration of BHMS graduates (Homepathy) who have completed the Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP) with the Maharashtra Medical Council (MMC).In a letter to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday, IMA Headquarters termed the government’s August 3 Government Resolution (GR) “illegal” and urged its immediate cancellation, arguing that it undermines medical education, violates established legal principles and poses a risk to public health.The controversy centres on the state’s decision to allow CCMP-qualified BHMS doctors to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council. The IMA has objected both to the CCMP course and to what it calls “dual medical council registration.”“The CCMP course has not been approved by the erstwhile Medical Council of India (MCI), the National Medical Commission (NMC), or the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH). Such a course cannot be considered valid and should be discontinued immediately,” the association said in its representation.The doctors’ body also argued that allowing practitioners to hold registrations under two different medical councils is unprecedented in India and could mislead patients regarding a doctor’s qualifications and scope of practice.The IMA further pointed out that the issue is already pending before the Bombay high court in a petition challenging amendments to the Maharashtra Medical Council Act. It said the government should not proceed with registrations while the matter remains sub judice.Questioning the state’s justification of addressing rural doctor shortages, the association claimed the circumstances have changed significantly since similar provisions were introduced over a decade ago.“The Maharashtra government has already done away with the compulsory rural bond system for MBBS graduates because of the non-availability of vacant posts, indicating that there is no longer a shortage of qualified allopathic doctors,” the letter stated.The association also said equating MBBS graduates, who undergo years of full-time medical education, with CCMP-trained practitioners who complete a part-time course would be unfair to students pursuing modern medicine.Citing the Supreme Court’s landmark judgment in Poonam Verma vs Ashwin Patel (1996), the IMA reiterated that practitioners registered in one recognised system of medicine cannot prescribe medicines or practise another system without recognised qualifications and valid registration in that system.The IMA warned that if the GR is not withdrawn and the CCMP course is not discontinued, it will call for a nationwide strike involving doctors of modern medicine, including medical students, resident doctors and interns across the country.Copies of the representation have also been sent to the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Union Health Minister and the Chairperson of the National Medical Commission.
Article Summary: The controversy centres on the state’s decision to allow CCMP-qualified BHMS doctors to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council. The IMA has objected both to the CCMP course and to what it calls “dual medical council registration”
